```{r}
#Argiope 
spiders <- read.csv("Argiope_fertilization_small.csv", header = TRUE)
#response variable: number of fertilized eggs
#explanatory variable: insertion time 
#covariates: male size, female size, eggs laid, and egg sacs produced

model <- lm(data = spiders, NumFertilized ~ InsertionDuration + MaleSize + FemaleSize + NumSacs + NumEggs)
summary(model)
# significant model! p=1.536e-14 overall and specifically both insertion duration and number of eggs are significant predictors (p = 0.008 and 4.09e-6 respectively). Insertion duration interesting appears to have a negative relationship with number of eggs fertilized while number of eggs understandably has a direct positive relationship with number fertilized (per the estimate ~ efect size ish) 
#adjusted R^2 = 0.6877, which is a decent correlation coefficient and fit for a model of this nature

plot(spiders$InsertionDuration, spiders$NumFertilized, pch = 20, col = "lightblue")
```

```{r}
#Quine
quine <- read.csv("quine.csv", header = TRUE)
#response variable: number of days absent (Days)
#explanatory variables: Ethnicity (Eth), Sex, Age, or Learner Status (Lrn)

model2 <- aov(Days ~ Eth + Sex + Age + Lrn, data = quine)
summary(model2)
#this summary does not give an overall p-value for model significance, but we can see from the ANOVA that ethnicity is highly significant as a predictor for absences (p = 0.000466), and Age also was significant (p = 0.031). 
#I don't immediately see anything from this summary that would indicate what kind of relationship these explanatory variables have with the response variable though.

#Tukey’s Honest Significant Differences
TukeyHSD(model2)
#based on this output, Ethnicity still appears to be highly significant with the difference between N and A ethnicities p = 0.0004658. Within age the only significant difference is between F2 and F1 (p = 0.0450841), while the other Age categories do not have significant differences in absences. 
#This is where you can find effect size/relationship information as "diff" as well as the 95% CI bounds. Not sure if I would be accurate in interpreting this as absences decreasing in ethnicity A compared to ethnicity N ??
```
